title: A hormone, a channel and a brake: melatonin orchestrates calcium signaling for aphid resistance
content: Aphids are among the most destructive pests worldwide. Beyond the direct damage caused by their piercing-sucking mouthparts (Burd and Burton 1992), these small insects can vector a diverse range of plant viruses (Züst and Agrawal 2016) and promote sooty mold colonization through their sugary honeydew secretions (Wilkinson et al. 1997). Understanding how plants naturally resist aphid attack is therefore of considerable agronomic importance. Plants perceive aphids primarily through salivary proteins, which trigger cell-surface receptor signaling. This includes calcium (Ca2+) influx, reactive oxygen species accumulation, activation of defense genes, and secondary metabolite biosynthetic enzymes (Züst and Agrawal 2016).
